content: LittleFS on ESP32 provides wear leveling and power-loss resilience and is fine for append-mostly logs, but true ring-buffer (overwrite-oldest) semantics perform poorly because rewriting the head of a file forces rewriting everything after it; metadata overhead can also exceed payload size for many tiny appends. Better pattern for GPS track logging: append fixed-size records to sequential files/segments (e.g. one file per session or per N records), keep a separate small NVS/LittleFS cursor file recording last-uploaded offset/segment, and rotate/delete old fully-uploaded segments instead of doing in-place ring-buffer overwrites.
